paper_title: Gas-rich dwarf galaxies as a new probe of dark matter interactions with ordinary matter
coupling_convention: dimensionless kinetic mixing parameter g (paper's notation, equivalent to chi for g<<1)
notes: Wadekar & Farrar (arXiv:1903.12190) derive new astrophysical bounds on ultra-light hidden-photon DM (kinetic mixing g) from requiring DM heating of Leo T dwarf galaxy gas not exceed its radiative cooling rate (Fig. 2), covering 1e-23 < m < 1e-10 eV. The figure axis values are garbled in the provided text, so the data points were analytically reconstructed from the paper's own formalism (Appendix E, Eqs. E2-E5) using stated parameters: average cooling rate C ~ 3.8e-30 erg/cm3/s, T ~ 6000 K, n_e ~ 1e-4 cm^-3 (giving omega_p ~ 3.7e-13 eV), rho_DM ~ 1.75 GeV/cm3. The bound scales as g ~ 1e-22/m[eV] for m << omega_p and g ~ m for m >> omega_p, with V-shape minimum g ~ 3e-10 near m ~ 4e-13 eV; crossover with CMB bounds near 1e-10 eV is consistent with the paper's statement. Points are order-of-magnitude reconstructions, not digitized values (exact data available at the paper's GitHub link). The paper also constrains millicharged DM and DM-nucleon/electron cross sections (not encoded here since the hidden-photon result is the headline exclusion matching the enum). No statistical CL quoted (heating-rate inequality argument).
